target_customer: Farmers, vineyards, orchards and agronomy service providers buying frequent aerial crop imagery
problem: Farmers needed timely high resolution crop imagery. Satellites lacked resolution and drones did not scale, so TerrAvion flew planes and delivered processed images overnight.
business_model: Subscription for aerial imagery priced per acre, sold directly and through agronomy partners

founders.name: Robert Morris
founders.background_notes: Per the YC page he led the Army's first drone platoon in Afghanistan.

founders.name: Cornell Wright
founders.background_notes: Named co-founder in the TechCrunch launch article, which says he holds a private pilot license.

exit.reason: TerrAvion ceased operations and filed for bankruptcy in 2020 per CropLife coverage seen in search results. AgroScout then bought the assets.

competitors.name: Ceres Imaging
competitors.funding_then: 3 million seed reported March 2014 by one aggregator

technical_complexity.rationale: Automating overnight image processing and flight operations across planes was hard for a small team, but used mostly off the shelf software per TechCrunch in 2014.

defensibility.rationale: Scale of flights and partner integrations helped, but imagery was a commodity that satellites and drones could erode.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent bought TerrAvion. AgroScout bought its assets in January 2022 after the company ceased operations in 2020.

market_need_then: The 2014 launch article priced single pass competing services at 6 to 15 dollars an acre and TerrAvion offered weekly imagery at 22 to 30 dollars an acre, targeting farms that wanted frequent imagery. No demand figures were stated.

branding.domain_note: Used terravion.com per the YC page.
branding.community_and_virality: Trade press coverage in AgFunderNews, TechCrunch and CropLife. No fan or merch evidence found.

brand_strength.rationale: Known within agtech trade press and a trademark was registered in 2015, but no evidence the name drove growth.

pivots.why: A Farm Progress article, per search coverage, says the founder scrapped drones in favor of aircraft

outcome_analysis: TerrAvion grew from a 2014 launch in California to flying over 20 million acres a week, per the AgroScout release, and raised a 10 million dollar Series A in February 2017. It abruptly ceased operations on September 4, 2020 and filed for bankruptcy per CropLife coverage, and AgroScout bought its assets in January 2022. The CEO's stated reason was not captured, so ran out of money is inferred from the bankruptcy.
notes: Company site terravion.com did not resolve in this session. The CropLife page returned 403, so the 2020 shutdown date and bankruptcy come from search result text. The seed in 2014 rests on one database (CB Insights, with Bouncewatch also listing undisclosed seeds in 2014 and 2015) and the investor list combines a search summary naming Y Combinator, Funders Club, Initialized and Grey Corp, so treat as unverified. CB Insights totals 11.17M over 7 rounds, above the 10M Series A, so about 1.17M of rounds are unrecorded. Ceres Imaging seed rests on one aggregator. GeoVantage was named biggest competitor only in a 2017 article, so it is not listed. The YC page states largest volume overnight imagery provider 2015 to 2020 while its description says since 2016. The asset sale is the exit, not a full company acquisition. The directory status Inactive is consistent with the 2020 shutdown, with the 2022 asset sale recorded as the exit.
